messages:
maya: Quick one / we have an IC relocating EU -> US same month as a proposed promo. Manager wants to shift effective date to avoid split payroll. Any hard rules?
leo: Payroll cutoffs differ by country. Best practice: keep promo in same calendar month when possible. Setting effective date to last day of origin month often reduces complexity. @samir can confirm.
samir: Correct. Last-day-of-month is allowed but will likely trigger retro calc in the new payroll. Equity timing is separate / comp ops must greenlight if you want grants aligned. Document any retro and loop payroll + comp ops.
maya: Manager also asked what to send back if evidence is thin. Do we have a boilerplate handback message?
people-ops-bot: See leveling checklist: https://intra.redwood/people-ops/leveling-checklist and template: /templates/leveling-evidence.md. Required: impact summary, 2+ examples with metrics, manager endorsement.
fran: Use the Promo Portal "return" flow (don't delete). Include targeted bullets of missing items and a 14-day resubmission window. Example bullets: 1) add 2 quantified examples; 2) attach feedback <6 months; 3) clarify scope vs peer group.
leo: Note on peer reviews: prefer <6 months; up to 9 months OK with manager rationale in comments. >9 months needs recent corroboration.
maya: Who signs exceptions? Manager said exec already ok verbally.
samir: Approval chain: Manager + Sr People Ops partner + Compensation. Exec verbal is context only / must attach written note and route for exception if needed.
fran: I'll paste a short handback template in the portal and post the snippet here when done.
leo: I'll ping payroll and comp ops about cutoff windows for the specific countries and post timing constraints.
maya: Thanks all :pray:
